LESSON: FICTION AND NON-FICTION 6.3.2 NON- FICTION: AUTOBIOGRAPHY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Fiction and Non-Fiction 6.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non-Fiction 6.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do language and style enhance the presentation of an autobiography?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the stylistic devices in an autobiography for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non-Fiction 6.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. discuss the language and style in the autobiography for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non-Fiction 6.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the significance of language and style in autobiographies for lifelong learning. ● Learners read an autobiography, ● In groups learners team up to identify stylistic devices used, ● Learners identify the point of view used in narration in the autobiography, ● In groups learners discuss the language and style in the autobiography, ● Learners make notes on the language and style in the autobiography, ● Learners their work for peer review, ● In groups learners discuss the influence that history and culture of How do language and style enhance the presentation of an autobiography? 57 Kenya have had on the autobiography.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non-Fiction 6.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: This is promoted as the learner reflects on their work when seeking feedback by sharing their work for

peer review.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner discusses the influence that history and culture of

Kenya have had on the autobiography.

Values:
● Integrity: This is promoted as the learner exhibits self- discipline in accomplishing tasks when reading an autobiography.

● Respect: This is developed as the learner positively regards others with dignity as they review each other’s work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: This is nurtured as the learner works jointly with peers to accomplish group goals.
